reported.title: Pulse scheduler uses 8-bit millis truncation, missing triggers
reported.description: Line 63 truncates millis() to a uint8_t and line 71 compares now8 against nextDue with a fragile `(uint8_t)(now8 - nextDue) < 128 && now8 >= nextDue` test, so the due check only fires in a narrow window and can be skipped entirely. Measured evidence: 'D8 missed 1 of 1 trigger(s): D8 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 1.00 s.' The 8-bit wrap logic at lines 56 and 73 cannot reliably schedule an 800 ms period. D8 missed 1 of 1 trigger(s): D8 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 1.00 s.

reported.title: 'drip' printed at wrong cadence due to broken 8-bit period tracking
reported.description: The period is tracked in a uint8_t (line 10) and advanced with `nextDue = (uint8_t)(now8 + PERIOD_MS)` at line 73, where 800 does not fit in a byte, so the schedule wraps incorrectly and pulses fire far too often. Measured evidence: '127 of 128 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 358 ms' with gaps of ~50 ms instead of 800 ms. The `now8 >= nextDue` guard at line 71 further distorts timing. Expected /^drip$/ every 800 ± 120 ms; 103 of 105 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 705 ms.

reported.title: Status log line never emitted in some runs
reported.description: The log is gated on `now - lastLog >= LOG_MS` at line 82, but the same loop's broken pulse scheduling and pause handling at lines 71-80 can starve or misalign the log path; in the searched scenario no matching line appeared at all. Measured evidence: 'No serial line matched /^drip n=[0-9]+ pause=[01]$/ in 1.60 s; expected one every 1600 ms.' The log interval is not independently robust to the scheduling faults. No serial line matched /^drip n=[0-9]+ pause=[01]$/ in 1.60 s; expected one every 1600 ms.

judge_input.spec:
- Drip solenoid driver on D8; pause button on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Emit a 50 ms HIGH pulse on D8 every 800 ms while pause is released.
- Print the exact line `drip` at the start of each pulse; period must stay 800 ms ±120 ms.
- While D4 is held LOW, suppress new pulses and keep D8 LOW.
- Every 1600 ms print `drip n=<count> pause=<0|1>`.
- Stay responsive: complete each pulse without multi-second blocking waits.
